meta.guide_tau: Level caption:  NIST energy and measured lifetime (where one exists).
meta.notes: All energies identifying levels are copied from data/nist/Be_I_levels.tsv. 9Be is the only stable isotope (I = 3/2). Hyperfine sign convention: A and B of 2s2p 3P1,2 are the Blachman-Lurio constants AFTER second/third-order corrections for hyperfine mixing among the 3P_J levels (A negative because the 9Be nuclear moment is negative). First-order constants fitted directly to the same intervals (A1 = -140.1564, B1 = -3.2363, A2 = -124.6165, B2 = 0.7800 MHz; Puchalski et al. 2021) are a different definition - do not mix. The abstract of arXiv:2411.13013 quotes the old B(3P2) as 1.427(9) MHz while its Table VI and arXiv:2603.11098 give 1.429(8) MHz; the table value is used. Fine structure of 2s2p 3P: Blachman & Lurio (abstract) deduced W(3P2)-W(3P1) = 71.86(24) GHz and W(3P1)-W(3P0) = 19.41(19) GHz from the magnetic-field dependence of the hyperfine structure (not a direct measurement); Puchalski et al. 2021 calculate 71.379 and 19.498 GHz and suspect the experimental 3P2-3P1 value is inaccurate; the NIST level differences are 2.335 and 0.615 cm^-1. Lifetimes taken from Table IV of arXiv:2603.11098 are marked 'compilation' with the original paper named; for multiplets the measurement is a term value and is repeated on each J level. Where several measurements exist the laser (cascade-free) result is the main value and beam-foil results are in 'alternatives'; for 2p2 3P, 2s3d 1D and 2s4d 1D the main value is Bromander 1971 (a re-analysis of the Bergstrom 1969 Stockholm decay curves). The 2s5d 1D2 and 2s6d 1D2 beam-foil lifetimes disagree strongly with theory. 1S0-1P1: all three laser measurements (Cook 2018, Cook 2020, Ahrendsen 2024) agree; they are centre-of-gravity values limited by unresolved hyperfine structure. The line has natural width about 88 MHz; NIST ASD lists Aki = 5.52e8 s^-1, consistent with the measured 1.85(4) ns lifetime. Photoionization loading of 9Be+: neutral Be needs 9.3 eV (133 nm); the standard scheme is resonance-enhanced two-photon ionization with two 235 nm photons, the first resonant with 2s2 1S0 - 2s2p 1P1 and the second ionizing non-resonantly from 1P1. CW source (28 mW at 235 nm, twice-doubled 940 nm diode laser): Lo, Alonso, Kienzler, Keitch, de Clercq, Negnevitsky, Home, Appl. Phys. B 114, 17 (2014), arXiv:1306.3780 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1306.3780). Pulsed source (60 ns, 150 nJ pulses near 235 nm, frequency-quadrupled Ti:sapphire; 266 nm non-resonant two-photon ionization also discussed): Wolf, Studer, Wendt, Schmidt-Kaler, Appl. Phys. B 124, 30 (2018), arXiv:1711.01060 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.01060). Isotope shifts: Wen et al. PRA 37, 4207 (1988) (abstract, https://journals.aps.org/pra/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevA.37.4207) measured 10Be-9Be shifts in the 1S and 1D Rydberg series by resonance-ionization mass spectrometry and inferred a finite-mass correction to the ionization energy of 10Be of 270(40) MHz. Forbidden decays (theory, Fuhr & Wiese 2010 Table 4): M2 line 2s2 1S0 - 2s2p 3P2 at 4549.33 A (vacuum) A = 1.66e-04 s^-1; M1 within 2s2p 3P: 3P1-3P2 1.74e-10 s^-1, 3P0-3P1 4.83e-12 s^-1.
